title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
"My sugars have been high lately."

History of Present Illness
The patient presents today for follow-up regarding management of their type 2 diabetes mellitus. They report feeling generally well but mention increased thirst and frequent urination over the last week. Review of recent logs shows several instances of hyperglycemia. The patient continues to take their prescribed insulin and metformin. They are concerned about the current level of hyperglycemia.

Medication List
Insulin (dosage and frequency not specified)
Metformin

Exam
Vitals stable. Skin exam unremarkable. Cardiovascular exam reveals regular rate and rhythm. Neurological exam is intact.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Currently presenting with hyperglycemia. The patient is on long-term management with insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent.
2. Hyperglycemia.

Plan
Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin. Follow up in three months. Patient educated on monitoring blood glucose levels and signs of hyperglycemia. Recommend reviewing blood glucose logs prior to next visit.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
